answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs at every transaction wharf. Validating a single identity is cheap, but scaling a swarm imposes exponential capital exhaustion where staking costs escalate superlinearly: identity churn becomes an unsustainable economic burden. A solitary node slips through like a zephyr, yet a swarm burns out like an overtaxed comet.
